nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-01.title: Product of all eight
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-01.body:
If each pair has product $p$, then $p^4$ is the product of all eight numbers, $2^{12}\cdot3^8\cdot5^4$. So $p=2^3\cdot3^2\cdot5=360$. Such a pairing exists: $\{72,5\},\{8,45\},\{24,15\},\{10,36\}$.

**Answer: 360**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-01.title: Largest with smallest
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-01.body:
All numbers are positive, so the largest number must be paired with the smallest (any other partner of $72$ would make that product bigger than the product with $5$ in it). Hence $p=72\cdot5=360$.

**Answer: 360**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-02.title: Angle bisectors
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-02.body:
Since $3^2+4^2=5^2$, $\angle C=90^\circ$. The incenter lies on the angle bisectors, so $\angle IAB+\angle IBA=\frac12(\angle CAB+\angle CBA)=\frac12\cdot90^\circ=45^\circ$, and $\angle AIB=180^\circ-45^\circ=135^\circ$.

**Answer: 135**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-03.title: Count grid-line crossings
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-03.body:
Tracing the diagonal, it enters a new square each time it crosses an interior grid line. There are $4+6=10$ interior grid lines, and since $\gcd(5,7)=1$ the diagonal never passes through an interior lattice point, so it crosses them one at a time. Starting in one square and entering $10$ more gives $11$ squares.

**Answer: 11**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-03.title: Formula
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-03.body:
An $m\times n$ rectangle's diagonal crosses $m+n-\gcd(m,n)$ unit squares: $5+7-1=11$.

**Answer: 11**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-04.title: Self-similarity
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-04.body:
Let $x$ be the value. Then $x=\sqrt{7+\sqrt{1+x}}$, so $x^2-7=\sqrt{1+x}$. Trying $x=3$: $9-7=2=\sqrt4$. ✓ For $x>\sqrt7$ the left side $x^2-7$ is increasing much faster than $\sqrt{1+x}$, and the two graphs cross only once there, so $x=3$.

**Answer: 3**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-04.title: Polynomial
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-04.body:
Squaring $x^2-7=\sqrt{1+x}$ gives $x^4-14x^2-x+48=0$, which factors as $(x-3)(x^3+3x^2-5x-16)=0$. The cubic has no root with $x^2\ge7$ (at $x=\sqrt7\approx2.65$ it is already positive and increasing), so the value is $3$.

**Answer: 3**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-05.title: By smallest element
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-05.body:
Such a subset is a block $\{a,a+1,\dots,b\}$ with $a<b$. With smallest element $1$ there are $9$ choices of $b$, with $2$ there are $8$, and so on: $9+8+\cdots+1=45$.

**Answer: 45**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-05.title: Choose the endpoints
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-05.body:
Each block is determined by its two distinct endpoints, so the count is $\binom{10}{2}=45$.

**Answer: 45**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-06.title: Power of a Point
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-06.body:
$T$ is on the radical axis $AB$, so $TP^2=TB\cdot TA=TQ^2$ and $TP=TQ=\frac12PQ$. Let $S$ and $R$ be the centers of the circles with radii $3$ and $5$. $SP$ and $RQ$ are perpendicular to $PQ$. Drawing the line through $S$ perpendicular to $RQ$, meeting it at $U$, gives $RU=5-3=2$ and $PQ=SU=\sqrt{6^2-2^2}=4\sqrt2$. So $PT=2\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt2$**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-07.title: Ordered then unordered
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-07.body:
Choose the first square in $25$ ways; the second must avoid its row and column, leaving $16$. Each set is counted twice, so there are $\frac{25\cdot16}{2}=200$.

**Answer: 200**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-07.title: Choose rows and columns
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-07.body:
Pick $2$ rows and $2$ columns: $\binom52^2=100$ ways; the two squares are on one of the $2$ diagonals of the resulting $2\times2$ arrangement. Total $200$.

**Answer: 200**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-08.title: Use the complement
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-08.body:
The whole set sums to $120$, so the complement $S'$ sums to $10$. A set of distinct positive integers with sum $10$ can have $1,2,3,$ or $4$ elements (e.g. $\{10\},\{1,9\},\{1,2,7\},\{1,2,3,4\}$), but not $5$ or more, since $1+2+3+4+5=15>10$. As $|S|=15-|S'|$, $n$ can be $14,13,12,11$.

**Answer: $11, 12, 13, 14$**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-09.title: Work backwards
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-09.body:
The volume doubles each second, so one second before reaching $800$ it was $400$: at $10-1=9$ seconds.

**Answer: 9**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-10.title: Self-similarity
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-10.body:
The expression repeats, so $2=\sqrt{a+\sqrt{b+2}}$, i.e. $4-a=\sqrt{b+2}$. Since $\sqrt{b+2}>\sqrt2$, $a\in\{1,2\}$: $a=1$ gives $b+2=9$, $b=7$; $a=2$ gives $b+2=4$, $b=2$. ($a=3$ would need $b=-1$.)

**Answer: $(1,7)$ and $(2,2)$**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-11.title: Exponents
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-11.body:
Each prime exponent in $N$ is a multiple of $4$ and of $6$, hence of $12$. So $N$ is a $12$th power, and the smallest one greater than $1$ is $2^{12}=4096$ ($a=8$, $b=4$).

**Answer: 4096**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-12.title: Rhombus
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-12.body:
Let $M,N$ be the midpoints of $AB$, $CD$, the centers; $MN=4$ and both radii are $3$, so $EMFN$ is a rhombus with perpendicular diagonals $MN$ and $EF$ meeting at $O$. In right triangle $MOF$, $OF=\sqrt{3^2-2^2}=\sqrt5$, so $EF=2\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt5$**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-12.title: Coordinates
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-12.body:
Put $M=(0,0)$, $N=(0,4)$. The circles $x^2+y^2=9$ and $x^2+(y-4)^2=9$ meet where $y=2$, $x=\pm\sqrt5$. So $EF=2\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt5$**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-14.title: Count cyclic orders
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-14.body:
A path through all six points is a cyclic ordering of them. Listing the vertices in the order traced gives one of $6!$ sequences, but each path is counted $6$ times (starting vertex) and $2$ times (direction). So there are $\frac{6!}{12}=60$.

**Answer: 60**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-15.title: Parity
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-15.body:
If the value were $0$, the numbers with plus signs (including $1$) would have the same sum as those with minus signs, so each sum would be $\frac{55}{2}$, not an integer. So no assignment works.

**Answer: 0**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-16.title: Along the diagonal
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-16.body:
Both centers lie on diagonal $AC$. Say the larger circle (radius $2x$, center $O$) is near $A$ and the smaller (radius $x$, center $P$) near $C$. Then $AO=2x\sqrt2$, $PC=x\sqrt2$, and $OP=3x$. So $\sqrt2=AC=2x\sqrt2+3x+x\sqrt2=3x(1+\sqrt2)$, and the sum of radii is $3x=\frac{\sqrt2}{1+\sqrt2}=2-\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $2-\sqrt2$**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-17.title: Sum by length
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-17.body:
There are $3^k$ sequences of length $k$, so $3+9+27+81=120$.

**Answer: 120**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-18.title: Exponent conditions
nyciml-2009-10-spring-junior-18.body:
Primes other than $2,3,5$ only make $n$ bigger, so let $n=2^a3^b5^c$. $10n=2^{a+1}3^b5^{c+1}$ is a square: $a$ odd, $b$ even, $c$ odd. $6n=2^{a+1}3^{b+1}5^c$ is a cube: $a\equiv2$, $b\equiv2\pmod3$, $3\mid c$. The smallest choices are $a=5$, $b=2$, $c=3$, so $n=2^5\cdot3^2\cdot5^3=36000$.

**Answer: 36000**
